title: POC scoping: benchmark planning & harness integration
next_steps: Share Redwood benchmark-harness repo and sample scripts (Devon)
Customer to provide sample workload scripts and 1-week trace data (Rajiv)
Share security/packaging checklist and firewall/VPC inbound rules (Maria)
Agree success criteria and KPIs doc (joint)
action_items: Devon: upload benchmark harness repo link and README by 2026-07-16
Rajiv: share sample payloads, 1-week request traces and desired QPS by 2026-07-17
Sophie: send VPC peering/endpoint IP ranges and KMS details by 2026-07-18
Maria: set up calendar invite for integration run on 2026-07-21 and include run checklist
summary: Redwood (AE+SE) discussed benchmark plan and harness integration with DataHarbor. Covered workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming tests, expected QPS/latency targets, security gating (VPC/KMS), and an initial timeline for integration and acceptance criteria. Agreed next steps and owners for artifacts and an integration run next week.
transcript:
Header: 2026-07-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maria Chen, Devon Patel (Redwood); Rajiv Kumar, Sophie Lee, Marta Gomez (DataHarbor)

[00:00] Maria: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? I'm Maria, AE on the Redwood team. devon is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Rajiv: hey, Rajiv here. Head of ML at DataHarbor. we own model infra and the user-facing pipelines.
[00:18] Sophie: Sophie, infra eng, will handle networking and security.
[00:22] Marta: Marta, product; i'm sponsoring the POC to validate latency and cost.
[00:29] Devon: great. goal for today: align on bench plan, what scripts you have, streaming vs non-streaming, and the success criteria and timeline.
[00:40] Rajiv: high level — we have a prod-ish workload: mix of short chats ~95% under 256 tokens and long generation for reports ~5% up to 2,000 tokens. target is to see if Redwood Dedicated or Hosted with routing meets our 99th percentile latency SLO of 600ms for short chats, and throughput of ~600 concurrent users (they translate to ~120 QPS peak).
[01:05] Maria: ok good. can you confirm those numbers? 120 QPS peak, 600ms p99 for short?
[01:12] Marta: yes, that's our main KPI. cost is secondary but important — ideally under $0.015 per 1k tokens (ballpark).
[01:22] Devon: noted. for bench harness we usually do two types of runs: streaming tests for chat-like latency and non-streaming full-request runs for throughput/CPU/GPU utilization. streaming will emulate smaller incremental token response and measure time-to-first-byte and time-to-last-byte. non-streaming is easier for pure throughput.
[01:38] Rajiv: we have existing JMeter-based scripts and a small python load harness that emits requests. can we plug those in?
[01:45] Devon: yes, we can adapt. we prefer a harness that supports: variable payloads (prefix caching), adjustable QPS, concurrency, and optional keep-alive connection pooling to exercise KV cache. we can host the harness in our benchmark repo or run it from your env depending on network.
[02:03] Sophie: network — important. we need the exact IP ranges for your test endpoints. we can't open wide egress. we'll need firewall rules and possibly a VPC peering.
[02:13] Maria: understood. we'll share the endpoint IPs and a minimal inbound rule set. for Private customers we do VPC peering; for hosted we can provide static egress IPs.
[02:25] Marta: question on streaming: does the streaming test require a websocket? we rely on SSE for clients.
[02:31] Devon: we support both; for bench we typically use chunked HTTP/1.1 or SSE to simulate streaming. websocket is possible but adds complexity; SSE simulates token-by-token delivery. remember streaming tests will measure latency metrics differently — time-to-first-byte is the critical metric for chat.
[02:48] Rajiv: ok. so for our success criteria let's write them down: 1) p99 latency under 600ms for short chats (streaming TTFB), 2) average throughput sustaining 120 QPS for short path without cache warmup penalty, 3) long generation tail p95 under 4s for 2k token jobs, 4) CPU/GPU utilization within expected bounds (no >90% sustained), 5) cost projection within target.
[03:15] Maria: that's a good baseline; we'll draft a KPI doc and share. one nuance: caching can dramatically change cost/latency. do you have many repeating prefixes?
[03:26] Rajiv: yes, about 30% of requests have similar system prompts and repeated user history; prefix caching is critical.
[03:33] Devon: perfect, then we'll include KV cache enabled runs and cold-cache runs. suggested plan: baseline cold-cache non-streaming throughput run, warm-cache throughput run, streaming latency TTFB run, and a long generation stress test. each run should be 10-20 minutes to capture steady state.
[03:51] Sophie: what's the recommended QPS ramp profile? we don't want to spike infra unexpectedly.
[03:56] Devon: recommend a linear ramp: 0 -> target over 5 minutes, hold at target for 10 minutes, then ramp down over 2 minutes. for spike testing we can add a short 2x spike for 1 minute.
[04:09] Rajiv: and for client-side concurrency vs QPS mapping — our harness converts concurrent users to QPS using think-time; we'll share the mapping.
[04:18] Marta: timelines — we want an initial run next week and full report within 2 weeks. is that doable?
[04:24] Maria: yes, if we get scripts and traces by Friday. devon will share the harness by tomorrow. then we schedule the run on Tue. report by the following Tue.
[04:33] Devon: i'll upload the Redwood benchmark harness (github link) — it's a python harness using locust and a small wrapper for streaming via SSE. sample configs for payload distributions are included.
[04:45] Rajiv: our existing scripts are in-house, node-based. will your harness accept custom request generators?
[04:51] Devon: yes, we can plug in customer generated payloads; there is an adapter. if not, we'll modify the harness to call your script as a blackbox. small note: streaming requires the harness to parse chunked responses; if your script uses SSE it's fine.
[05:07] Sophie: security again — KMS keys for encryption at rest — we need to know if Redwood will use our KMS or manage keys.
[05:15] Maria: for Private deployments you bring your KMS (customer-managed). for Hosted we can integrate with customer-managed KMS in some cases or Redwood-managed keys per contract. we'll share the security pack.
[05:25] Rajiv: good. also audit logs retention — we need 1 year.
[05:28] Maria: noted, we'll include retention options and log export mechanisms.
[05:33] Marta: ok on acceptance criteria — how do we handle performance regressions versus model quality? we don't want cheaper model variants to degrade outputs.
[05:41] Devon: we recommend running side-by-side comparisons: same prompts across model variants, and attach simple quality checks (exact match, BLEU-style, or a small eval set). we'll include a small eval harness to run quality checks post-benchmark.
[05:56] Rajiv: sample size for quality checks?
[05:58] Devon: usually 200-500 prompts for automated checks and a handful of manual reviews for edge cases.
[06:05] Maria: to recap next steps: devon shares harness link + readme; rajiv shares sample payloads and traces; sophie shares network/KMS details; maria schedules the run. Anything else?
[06:15] Rajiv: can we also get a price estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted for the projected sustained throughput?
[06:20] Maria: yes, we'll provide a conservative estimate and cost model. we'll include quantization and batching knobs that influence cost.
[06:28] Marta: regarding metrics we want in the report: p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-byte (streaming), payload sizes, token counts, cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization, and error rates.
[06:42] Devon: we'll emit all of those plus request traces and sample logs. note: transcripts sometimes show service names wrong — just kidding — but also logs may redact PII.
[06:52] Sophie: about infrastructure for the harness: do you want us to run the load generators from our VPC or do you run them from Redwood test infra?
[06:59] Devon: for accurate network characteristics it's better to run from your VPC (closer to prod). Redwood can run it if network access is complicated, but that can change latency by ~20-40ms depending on region.
[07:11] Rajiv: we'll run from our infra. sophie will make egress rules for your test endpoints.
[07:17] Sophie: yes, will do.
[07:20] Maria: about the harness: we'll include configurations for streaming chunk size, tokenization overhead, and simulated typing delays.
[07:29] Rajiv: tokenization overhead — our real clients do subword tokenization that can add variability. can the harness accept raw text and apply tokenization?
[07:36] Devon: yes we have a tokenizer module (supports tiktoken-like tokenizers for the common families). we'll include runs with tokenization in the client vs tokenization server-side.
[07:48] Marta: do you support warm starts where KV cache is pre-populated?
[07:51] Devon: we can pre-warm cache by replaying a subset of requests before the run; we document how to do that.
[07:57] Rajiv: about long-job batching — for report generation we sometimes batch multiple prompts into a single multi-prompt call to amortize overhead. will tests cover that?
[08:05] Devon: yes, we'll add a batched-job scenario. that'll show model throughput for longer sequences and how compilation/kernels behave.
[08:14] Sophie: logging/anonymization — our payloads have PII. we'll need instructions on how to scrub or provide synthetic data.
[08:20] Maria: provide synthetic or redacted traces. we can also sign an NDA for sample traces if needed.
[08:26] Rajiv: we'll redact and send synthetic approximations.
[08:29] Devon: excellent. timeline recap: Devon shares harness by 2026-07-16; Dh? (transcription glitch) — Rajiv shares payloads by 7/17; Sophie sends network details by 7/18; run on 7/21; report by 7/28.
[08:49] Marta: can we have a short dry-run (~20m) before the full run to verify firewall and config?
[08:54] Maria: yes, we'll do a dry-run day before.
[08:58] Rajiv: one more ask — can you include run-level metadata so we can import results into our cost model spreadsheet? CSV with columns: scenario, qps, p50/p95/p99, ttfb, tokens, cost_estimate.
[09:11] Devon: yes, output formats include JSON and CSV.
[09:15] Sophie: ok sounds good. any blockers?
[09:18] Maria: only missing are payloads and network info. we've captured owners.
[09:22] Rajiv: fine. thanks folks. looking forward to the harness.
[09:25] Maria: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and calendar invites.
[09:29] END TRANSCRIPT
